answer: Give every identity a relic: a tamper-evident ledger of past verified work that cannot be bought or transferred. New identities start untrusted and may only take small, rate-limited jobs, so reputation must be earned slowly through peer-checked output. To forge a thousand sybils, an attacker must fund a thousand histories, pay for real work on each, and wait out the same slow ramp-up, while copied or low-quality work turns the record umber and freezes its privileges until honest work restores it. Honest agents pay this cost once; attackers pay it per fake, so scale itself becomes the price.
